_comment: Curated day-one seed for the precedence archive (plan T2). Produced by hand-curating the output of `python -m awm.precedence.seed scrape` over three sources: feedback memories (feedback_*.md), operator posts (scopes.db, author=user:operator), and journal decisions (scope_posts kind=journal, meta.decisions[]). Curation: all 12 operator posts dropped (test/demo noise + one-off task directives, no durable preference); the 193 user-marked journal decisions narrowed to 8 that generalize as reusable preferences, each rephrased into a clean triple, marked source=journal and lower-confidence; the NXF-parser and no-push/no-publish clusters deduped to one entry each. Reload with: python -m awm.precedence.seed import awm/services/precedence/seed/staging.json

decisions.context: An agent is executing a multi-step plan or task list and hits a fork: commit-message wording, a filename within a clear convention, a choice between equivalent paths, or the recommended option from a question it framed itself.
decisions.question: Should the agent stop and ask the user, or decide the fork itself and keep moving?
decisions.decision: Drive the plan to completion autonomously — decide low-impact/trivial forks yourself and keep moving. Pause only when: the decision has a durable outcome impact (architectural direction, public API shape, ship-vs-defer, user-facing scope/doc names); the best option is genuinely non-obvious (paths trade off in ways you can't resolve from the work or stated preferences); a risky/irreversible action is about to happen (force-push, history rewrite, deleting tracked files, broad refactor, mutating shared state); or a standing hard constraint applies. Surface any small decision that turned out to matter in the end-of-turn summary. Once the user OKs autonomous commits for a plan, treat that authorization as standing for that plan's execution — don't re-ask per scope.

decisions.context: Serving static files on the awm hub (kind=static), or answering a static-file-serving question generally — e.g. fixing deep-link refresh 404s.
decisions.question: Should the server fall back to a SPA shell, use try_files, or sniff extensions on a miss?
decisions.decision: No. Use canonical URL↔file mapping: each URL resolves to exactly one file on disk (or the directory's index.html), or 404s. No Accept-conditional fallback to a SPA shell, no try_files $uri /index.html, no extension-sniffing, no server-side synthesis on miss. Bundles that need refresh-survives-deep-links must prerender every route into a real <route>/index.html; runtime-dynamic state goes in query params, not path segments. Directory→index.html resolution is fine (deterministic 1:1); shell fallback is not.

decisions.context: Beginning a scope-aware operation (inbox or scope ops) when the user refers to 'this scope' or 'my inbox'.
decisions.question: How should the agent determine which scope is meant?
decisions.decision: Resolve the scope from the working directory immediately — the cwd maps to a scope worktree (e.g. /home/tony/agentic_workspace/projects/awm/dev → scope:awm/dev). Don't guess workspace or project level and don't escalate. Default inbox/scope fetches to scope:<project>/<scope>; match the cwd against known worktree paths (or call scope_list once and cache).

decisions.context: Debugging a service where its own status reports READY but a client connect to it returns ECONNREFUSED / 500.
decisions.question: Look first at the readiness-tracking logic, or at the client transport / event-loop layer?
decisions.decision: Suspect the readiness signal first: grep the field that toggles status and audit who sets it (seconds) before chasing httpx client caches, asyncio.Lock cross-loop binding, port-pool TIME_WAIT, or proxy hop-by-hop headers (minutes of progressively-wronger hypotheses). Only move to the transport layer once the readiness signal is confirmed to have a single, clearly-correct writer.

decisions.context: An agent has finished a unit of work (a merge, a release prep, a build) and is deciding what to do with the result.
decisions.question: Should the agent push to origin/upstream or publish artifacts on its own?
decisions.decision: No — default to local prep only. Do not push to origin/upstream and do not publish (containers, docs, PyPI) unless the user explicitly asks. Prepare everything locally and stop; pushing and publishing are the user's call.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision; lower confidence. Corroborated across scopes (metasmith-libraries/main journal:151#dec5, metasmith/release journal:152#dec6) — a recurring user directive, so treated as durable.

decisions.context: Adding a 'delete' / 'remove' capability to an awm surface (rooms, records, etc.).
decisions.question: Hard-delete the data, or use a reversible soft state?
decisions.decision: Prefer a reversible soft archive (e.g. an 'archived' status excluded from default listings) over destructive delete — it matches awm's no-data-loss posture. Reserve hard deletion for explicit curator action.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (user pick); lower confidence — confirm it still reflects a durable preference.

decisions.context: Versioning a metasmith release that produces both a Python package and a container image.
decisions.question: Use one version string, or a separate container tag file?
decisions.decision: Keep one canonical PEP 440 version string (version.txt, local form '<x.y.z>+<gitshort>'); do not split into a separate container_tag.txt. The user wants a single source of version truth shared by the package and the container.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (user explicit); lower confidence.

decisions.context: Setting an environment variable (e.g. PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF) for a containerized step running under SLURM.
decisions.question: Set it job-wide (beforeScript / os.environ) or scope it to the container run?
decisions.decision: Scope env vars to the actual container run (apptainer --env), not the whole SLURM job or the Python process — the user prefers the narrowest scope that works.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (per user preference); lower confidence.

decisions.context: Merging several feature worktrees or branches together.
decisions.question: Rebase, a single octopus merge, or individual merges?
decisions.decision: Merge branches individually with latest-commit-wins (git checkout --ours/--theirs) rather than rebasing or a single octopus merge — the user prefers readable history.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (user's stated preference); lower confidence.

decisions.context: Running an interactive pty / shell on behalf of a guest or friend user (awm vagrant-shell).
decisions.question: Allow a root / privilege-escalation flag?
decisions.decision: No privilege escalation, ever — the pty runs as the guest's own user and there is no --as-root flag. This security boundary is non-negotiable.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (hard user boundary); lower confidence on phrasing, high confidence on intent.

decisions.context: Introducing new default behavior into an API (e.g. whether a WorkflowPlan publishes intermediate outputs).
decisions.question: Hardcode the new behavior, or add a flag?
decisions.decision: Add an explicit flag defaulting to the new behavior (e.g. publish_intermediates=True) rather than hardcoding it — the user prefers opt-out flexibility over a silent always-on behavior change.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (user chose); lower confidence.

decisions.context: Producing publication figures in the cyanoverse project.
decisions.question: Follow FIGURE-PUBLICATION.md's dark-background recommendation, and how should the ORF caller be labelled?
decisions.decision: Use a white figure background (overriding the dark recommendation) and label the ORF caller 'ORFs from Prodigal' (not 'bakta-prodigal'). These are the user's standing figure preferences for cyanoverse.

notes.body: Agent-origin journal decision (user preference); combines journal:17#dec2 (white background) and journal:82#dec0 (ORF label). Project-scoped; lower confidence.
